author_notes: Slot slot_157 targets steven-tey/weathergpt, a runnable Next.js WeatherGPT app served offline with deterministic canned weather fixtures (no external network). The native lever is the app's own Ask WeatherGPT prompt explorer — a category filter (All / Forecast / Travel / Alerts) over eight example weather-prompt cards with a live 'Showing N · Category' readout, rendered below the weather cards on the home and city routes. The task repairs four defects on this explorer: a mobile horizontal-overflow regression (fixed-width nowrap tab and prompt-card tracks push the 390px viewport far past its width), illegible near-white prompt-card text with overlapping shingled cards, the explorer missing from some city routes, and a stale category filter whose readout freezes on 'Showing all 8 prompts'. The reference reflows the layout to zero mobile overflow, restores legible dark-on-light prompt cards, renders the explorer on every route, and wires the filter so the readout and visible cards track the active category. Graded assets include the logo.png and bg-light.png shell imagery and the prompt-card illustration surface. The leg-varying files are the Ask explorer component (ask-explorer.tsx), its stylesheet (ask-explorer.css), and the route-presence whitelist in page-data.tsx.
design_constraints: Keep the original WeatherGPT centered app shell, large heading, pill link, illustration graphic, Vercel/Next footer, and light background image treatment.
The Ask WeatherGPT explorer must stay a native prompt browser inside the WeatherGPT page (category tabs + readout + prompt cards), not a separate landing page, dashboard, or error document.
Preserve the home and London/Tokyo/New York routes including visible location names and temperature cards from the deterministic fallback data.
Desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile states must avoid horizontal overflow while keeping the explorer tabs, prompt cards, heading, weather cards, and footer readable.
The prompt cards must read as clean, legible cards with visible surfaces and dark text on the light ground; the category filter must drive both the visible cards and the live readout.

metadata.design_goal: repair the Ask WeatherGPT prompt explorer (mobile overflow, card legibility, cross-route presence, and live category filter) while keeping unrelated states stable
metadata.source_repo_kind: Next.js WeatherGPT plugin demo with deterministic canned weather, server-rendered routes, a native prompt explorer with a category filter, public logo/background assets, an illustration, and a Vercel/Next footer.

problem_statement: WeatherGPT is a Next.js weather-plugin demo you query with natural-language prompts. An 'Ask WeatherGPT' prompt explorer was added below the weather cards: a category tab row (All / Forecast / Travel / Alerts) that filters eight example prompt cards and a live readout that reads 'Showing all 8 prompts' and updates to 'Showing N · <Category>' as you pick a category. The explorer ships broken in four ways. (1) On the 390px mobile viewport its tab row and prompt-card track are fixed-width nowrap flex rows, forcing the document far wider than the viewport (horizontal overflow). (2) The prompt cards lose their surface and their text is set to near-white greys on the white page ground, so every prompt is illegible, and negative margins shingle the cards so they overlap into an unreadable pile. (3) The explorer only renders on some routes, not on every city route. (4) Clicking a category tab toggles the active pill but the readout stays frozen on 'Showing all 8 prompts' and the cards are never filtered. Repair the explorer so it reflows within the mobile viewport, the prompt cards are readable and laid out cleanly, the explorer appears on the home route and every city route, and picking a category filters the cards and updates the readout live — while keeping the WeatherGPT shell, canned weather cards, and footer unchanged.
required_content: On the 390px mobile explorer state, the Ask WeatherGPT tab row and prompt-card grid must reflow within the viewport so the document has no horizontal overflow beyond the 24px tolerance.
The eight prompt cards must be legible and laid out cleanly (readable text on visible card surfaces, no overlapping/shingled cards) in the desktop and mobile explorer states.
The Ask WeatherGPT explorer must render on the home route and on every city route (London, Tokyo, New York), not just a subset.
Selecting the Travel category must filter the prompt cards and update the live readout to 'Showing 3 · Travel'; the pre-click readout is 'Showing all 8 prompts'.

Keep the WeatherGPT title, ChatGPT Plugin description, Deploy your own to Vercel link, Your Location and Current Temperature cards, per-route canned weather data, Vercel Edge Runtime line, and Source link present and unchanged by the repair.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial capture the home route app shell.
desktop_london, desktop_tokyo, and desktop_new_york capture route-specific canned data and confirm the Ask WeatherGPT explorer is present on every city route.
desktop_explorer and mobile_explorer scroll the home route to the Ask WeatherGPT explorer so the prompt-card layout and legibility are verified on desktop and at 390px width.
desktop_explorer_travel clicks the Travel category tab and verifies the filtered cards plus the live 'Showing 3 · Travel' readout, changed from the pre-click 'Showing all 8 prompts'.
desktop_footer scrolls the London route to confirm the Vercel/Next footer and Source link survive the repair; mobile_london verifies the shell on a location route at 390px width.
All states are captured from the production build/start path.
